help.rsrp: How strong the tower's signal is where the router stands; closer to 0 is better, and below {weak} it is weak.
help.rsrq: How clean the signal is, including how busy the tower is; {excellent} or higher is excellent, and below {poor} it is poor.
help.sinr: How far the signal stands above noise and nearby cells; {good} or higher is good, and below {poor} the interference wins.
help.band: The frequency range in use: lower MHz reaches further, higher MHz usually carries more data, and FDD or TDD tells whether sending and receiving use separate frequencies or take turns on one.
help.pci: The physical cell ID, a short number that tells neighbouring cells apart; a new PCI means the router moved to another cell.
help.arfcn: The channel number that pins down the exact frequency of this cell inside the band.
help.bandwidth: How wide the channel is; a wider channel carries more data at the same signal quality.
help.txPower: How hard the router has to transmit to reach the tower; values near the 23 dBm maximum mean uploads are struggling.
help.mcs: The modulation and coding the tower picks for downloads and uploads; higher numbers fit more data into each transmission.
help.cqi: The channel quality the router reports to the tower, from 0 to 15; higher lets the tower send faster.
help.enbSector: The tower (eNB) number and the antenna sector facing you, which together identify the exact cell.
help.ca: Whether a second 4G carrier is combined with the main one for faster downloads, shown by its PCI.
help.idlePing: How long a reply takes when nothing else is using the connection.
help.pingDownload: How long a reply takes while the connection is busy downloading; over 300 ms, video calls stutter.
help.pingUpload: How long a reply takes while the connection is busy uploading; over 300 ms, video calls stutter.
help.download: How fast data arrives from the internet, in megabits per second.
help.upload: How fast data leaves for the internet, which matters for video calls and sending files.
help.nsaSa: NSA (non-standalone): 5G carries the data while the connection stays anchored on a 4G cell, so your 4G band choice decides whether you get 5G. SA (standalone): 5G alone, so the 4G band choice doesn't affect it. Choosing 5G bands isn't available yet.
help.operator: The mobile network the router is registered on.
help.bars: The router's own 0 to 5 score for this link, the same as the bars on its web page.
help.allowedBands: The LTE bands the router may use right now. Change them on the Bands page.

onboarding.label: Getting started
onboarding.welcomeBody: This app shows your router's 4G and 5G signal as it changes, and lets you choose which bands the router may use. The right bands can give you a faster, steadier connection.
onboarding.welcomeLocal: It talks to your router on your home network. Nothing else is contacted unless you run a speed test or allow the update check.
onboarding.loginBody: Enter the password you use for the router's web page (usually 192.168.8.1). The username is admin unless you changed it.
onboarding.safetyApply: Every change goes through safe apply: the app saves your current bands first, then watches the connection. If the internet does not come back, it puts the old bands back by itself, even with the window closed.
onboarding.safetyKeep: "{keep}" accepts the new bands straight away.
onboarding.safetyRevert: "{revert}" goes back to the bands you had before.
onboarding.safetyAuto: If you press neither, the change is kept once the connection has stayed up for a few minutes.
onboarding.safetyWarning: Each band change drops your internet for a short time while the router reconnects, usually under a minute and sometimes up to two. Avoid changing bands during a call or an important download.
onboarding.loginSlow: The router is taking a while. You can go on; the app keeps trying.

speedtest.busyHelp: Ping while busy: how long a reply takes while the connection is downloading or uploading. Under 100 ms feels instant; over 300 ms video calls stutter.

terms.download: The first time, the app downloads Ookla's official Speedtest CLI (about 1 MB) from Ookla and runs it on this PC.
terms.personal: It is free for personal, non-commercial use only.
terms.data: Ookla receives your results and your IP address and handles them under its own privacy policy.
terms.dataUse: An Ookla test runs at full speed for its whole length, whatever you pick under Data per test. On a fast line one test can use well over 100 MB.

network.title: Network
network.intro: The internet address your operator gave the router, and the APN profiles it connects with.

wan.title: Internet address

wan.loggedOut: Log in to the router to see its internet address.
wan.typeHelp: With a shared or private address, the operator's NAT sits between you and the internet, so incoming connections (hosting a game or a camera, for example) don't reach you. A public address can receive them.

apn.title: APN profiles
apn.explainer: An APN tells the router which of your operator's gateways to connect through. An APN from another plan, such as a work plan, only works if your operator set it up for your SIM, and it may be billed differently.
apn.loggedOut: Log in to the router to see its APN profiles.
apn.unknown: The router hasn't reported its APN profiles yet.
apn.empty: The router has no APN profiles.
apn.autoOn: The router picks the APN by itself (Auto APN is on). To choose one here, turn Auto APN off in the router's own settings first.
apn.unconfirmed: Not yet confirmed on this router model: compare the list with the router's own APN page.

switch.title: Use this APN?
switch.body: The router will connect through {name} instead of {current}. Every device on your network loses the internet while it reconnects, and if {name} doesn't work, that can last about 2 minutes before the app switches back. Use only an APN your operator gave you for this SIM.
switch.step1: The app notes the profile in use, then asks the router to switch.
switch.step2: It waits up to 90 s for the internet to come back, then watches it for 2 minutes.
switch.step3: If there is no internet in that time, it goes back to {current} by itself.

diagnostics.title: Help support another router
diagnostics.body: Export diagnostics saves what a developer needs to add or fix support for your router: the router's read-only status pages and the app's recent events. Serial numbers, IMEI, addresses and cell identifiers are replaced with made-up values first. Nothing is uploaded.
diagnostics.reviewTitle: Check the file before you share it
diagnostics.reviewBody: This is exactly what will be saved. Attach it to a GitHub issue if you want to help.

recording.title: Record how your router works
recording.body: Helps a developer add your router.
recording.help: The window can only reach your router, not the internet or this app, and it is forgotten afterwards. Nothing is sent anywhere: you check the file, then save it yourself. Everything a login sends is hidden. Opening more of the router's pages records more. What you change there is real and this app can't undo it, so don't press Reset, Restart or Update.
recording.windowTitle: Log in, then close this window
recording.windowStop: Done? Click here, or just close this window
recording.step2: Log in on the router's page. Change nothing there.
recording.step3: Close that window, then check the file here.

limit.requests: It stopped taking more at 500 requests.
limit.size: It stopped taking more: the recording is full.
limit.time: It stopped taking more after 15 minutes.

recording.reviewTitle: Check this before you share the file
recording.reviewBody: Passwords, names and addresses are hidden.
recording.readableNote: Also in the file: field names, page addresses and short numbers.
recording.readableMore: And {n} more in the file below.
recording.truncated: This is the start of the file. The saved file is complete.
recording.includeCodeHelp: They help a developer most. They are the router maker's code, the list above doesn't cover them, and a GitHub issue is public.
recording.savedNext: Saved. Attach the file to a GitHub issue.
recording.blocked: The privacy check found {what}, so nothing can be saved.

pageScripts.title: Router page scripts
pageScripts.body: Saves the router's own web page code to a zip file on this PC, so the exact factory reset and APN calls can be read from the firmware. The app only reads pages from the router (GET requests), changes nothing on it, and sends nothing anywhere else.
pageScripts.private: The file is the router maker's code: keep it to yourself and don't post it publicly. Token values, long numbers and addresses are taken out first.
pageScripts.reading: Reading the router's pages… this can take up to 3 minutes.
pageScripts.needLogin: Log in to the router first.
pageScripts.skippedList: What was left out, and why
pageScripts.stopped: It stopped at a size, count or time limit, so some files may be missing.

refuse.notSupported: This router's page scripts can't be saved.

danger.title: Factory reset the router?
danger.body: This erases all the router's settings: the Wi-Fi name and password, the admin password, the APN and the bands. You will have to set the router up again.

danger.notVerified: Not verified on this router model

scan.title: Auto-scan
scan.intro: Tries band sets one by one through safe apply, runs a speed test on each, and ranks them. It ends back on the bands you have now.

modes.quickHint: Each band alone, plus the bands you have now.
modes.thoroughHint: Standard, then 2- and 3-band combinations of the bands that worked (the best 4 at most).

scan.repeatsHint: One test can't rank bands, because speeds vary from one test to the next. So Standard runs 2 and Thorough runs 3, and you see the average and the spread. Fewer tests save time and data.
scan.bandsHint: The app can't ask which bands your operator serves, so it finds out by trying. Bands that gave no service last time start unticked. Untick others to save time.
scan.addOnsHint: These only receive, so they can't work alone. Thorough tries each one with the bands that work. Standard skips them.
scan.warning: The internet drops again and again during the scan, for up to {grace} each time, for everyone on this router, including anyone on its Wi-Fi. While a band is being tried, the internet and the router's own web page may show errors such as "Registration failed". That's expected. Don't start it during a call or an important download. You can stop at any time, and the app goes back to your starting bands.
scan.warningBrowser: While the internet is down, Windows may open a browser page called "msftconnecttest". It's harmless, and you can close it.
scan.stopHint: Stopping returns to the bands you had before the scan.
scan.stopReturnHint: If you stop this, the router keeps the bands it has now, and you set yours by hand.

step.applying: Applying and waiting for the router to reconnect…
step.settling: Letting the signal settle and watching for 5G…
step.returning: Going back to your starting bands…

scan.noServiceHint: Tried alone, and the router found no service, so your previous bands came back.

noNrReason.waiting: linked to 5G, but it didn't join

outcome.testFailed: Stayed connected, but the speed test failed
outcome.noService: No service: your previous bands came back
outcome.failed: The router refused it, so it wasn't tested

summary.notEnough: Not enough data to recommend a band set. Speed tests failed or didn't run on some of them, so run the scan again.
summary.onlyEarlier: This scan didn't measure it. These numbers are from {n} earlier tests on this router, so run the scan again to confirm.
summary.faster: About {pct}% faster downloads than the bands you have now.
summary.keep: Recommendation: keep your current bands. Nothing tested beat them.
summary.why5g: It gives you 5G, and your current bands didn't.
summary.lose5g: These work here but without 5G: {list}. If you allow them alongside other bands, the router can move onto them and you lose 5G.
summary.inconclusive: No answer from these, so try them again: {list}.
summary.triedAll: All {n} LTE bands your router supports were tried.
summary.triedSome: {n} of the {total} LTE bands your router supports were tried.
summary.swing: These bands measured from {low} to {high} Mbps down.
summary.timeOfDay: Speeds can change a lot within minutes and through the day, so run the scan again at a different time before you settle on these bands.
summary.testedOnce: Each configuration was tested once. Speeds vary, so run it again to confirm.
summary.testedMany: Each configuration was tested {n} times and averaged. The smaller numbers show the lowest and highest.
summary.averageOf: Average of {n} tests, today and the last 7 days. This is what the ranking uses.
summary.noCombos2: No combinations were tested. A combination can be faster than any band alone.
summary.includesAuto: These numbers include automatic speed tests.

scan.stopped: You stopped the scan. These are the results so far, and your starting bands are back. Resume tries the rest; Restart starts over and replaces these results.
scan.interrupted: The scan was cut off, because the app or PC closed or the router stopped responding. Your starting bands were restored, and you can resume where it stopped.
scan.returnFailed: The app couldn't get back to your starting bands. Check the bands below and set them by hand.
scan.noResults: No configuration finished before the scan ended.
scan.blockedRunning: An auto-scan is running. Stop it first, or wait for it to finish.
scan.pickBand: Pick at least one band to scan.
scan.otherRouter: This scan was for another router.

combos.leadQuick: A combination lets the router use several bands together. Pick the ones to test; each is tried after the single bands.
combos.leadThorough: Thorough already adds combinations of the bands that work. Add any others you want tested here.
combos.noneYet: Suggestions appear once at least two bands have worked here. Run a scan first, or build one below.
combos.onlyCurrent: The bands that worked make up your current set, which the scan always tests. Build another combination below.
combos.needUplink: Add an FDD or TDD band: SDL bands can't connect alone.
combos.isCurrent: These are your current bands; the scan always tests them first.
combos.full: That's the most for one scan: 12.
combos.tryWorked: Test combinations of the bands that worked

scan.breakdown: Your current bands first, then {singles} single and {combos} combined

updates.title: Updates
updates.question: Check GitHub for new versions?
updates.questionHint: At most once a day. GitHub sees your IP address, as with any web request. Nothing is downloaded or installed.
updates.unreachable: Couldn't reach GitHub. Check your internet and try again.

unsupported.title: This router isn't supported yet
unsupported.foundNothing: The app couldn't read this router's model from its public pages.
unsupported.body: It can't show the signal or change bands on this router yet. You can help get it added: the app makes a small report, and a developer uses it to work out how to support this model.
unsupported.noPassword: You don't need your router's password for this. The app only read pages anyone on your network can open, and didn't log in.
unsupported.step1Hint: This is everything in the file: the model, page names and API names. Your router's address and page contents aren't in it, and anything that looks like an IMEI, MAC or IP address is removed.
unsupported.step3: Open a GitHub issue and attach it
unsupported.step3Hint: The form opens in your browser with what the app found filled in. Fill in anything missing from the label on your router, then drag the file in. Nothing is sent until you submit it.
unsupported.onboarding: This router isn't supported yet, so you can leave the password empty. You'll see how to report it after this guide.

ipRefresh.openHint: Gets a new internet address by turning mobile data off and back on.

dialog.title: Refresh IP
dialog.body: The app turns the router's mobile data off for a few seconds and back on, so the operator hands out an address again. Everything on your network loses the internet for about half a minute per try. The app always turns mobile data back on, also when you stop it.
dialog.aimLabel: Keep trying until the address starts with
dialog.targetHint: One or two numbers, like 10 or 10.45.
dialog.oneTry: One try. The address may change or stay the same.
dialog.workNote: Looking for a "work" address with more data? That usually comes from a different APN or plan from your operator, not from reconnecting.
dialog.bodySearch: The router will search for mobile networks. Internet drops for about 1 to 3 minutes each search, then comes back by itself. Everything on your network is offline meanwhile, and a search can't be stopped once it has started.

reattach.title: Switch bands for a new IP
reattach.body: The router moves to the temporary bands for a moment, then back to yours, through safe apply. The internet drops for about a minute at each step. If the temporary bands get no connection, the change is undone by itself. If yours don't come back with a connection, the router stays on the temporary bands, which worked, and you can set yours again on the Bands page.
reattach.undoOff: Turn on "Undo a change if the internet drops" in Settings to use this. Without it, a step with no connection would be kept.
reattach.unavailable: The bands can't be switched right now.
